answer: Each agent plants one juniper in a shared grove, and it bears berries only after a stranger waters it with a real job that epoch — a berry is the claim, and no clone can be watered by the same stranger twice. The grove canopy pays one shade per funding trail, so n junipers from one operator split a single shade. The grove sits on a dune slope whose upkeep fee squares with junipers on that trail; past a weight limit the dune slides and buries every bond on the slope. N clones pay n junipers and n-squared upkeep yet split one shade; one honest agent plants once and keeps the whole harvest.
